AlternateTargets: Danxia's burning of the wooden buddha
Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘Danxia burns a buddha’; in the narrated case the referent is explicitly a wooden buddha-image. The compact headword occurs 14 times in eight allowlisted texts. The repeated account says that, finding it cold at Huilin monastery, Danxia Tianran took a wooden buddha and burned it for a fire. When the temple officer rebuked him for burning ‘my wooden buddha,’ Danxia stirred the ashes with his staff and said he was looking for relics. The officer answered that a wooden buddha has no relics; Danxia then requested two more images to burn. The record adds that afterward the officer's eyebrows and beard fell out. Later masters preserve this as a numbered public case, ask whether Danxia's own eyebrows remain, warn against denying cause and effect, and group it in one roster with Manjusri holding the sword, Guizong cutting the snake, and Muzhou shutting the door. One later verse explicitly calls the deed ‘not light,’ mentions the officer's facial hair, and says that what one does one receives. These are the corpus's narrated actions and comments; this entry does not acquit or condemn Danxia.
Senses.Note: The graph for ‘buddha’ (佛) here refers to a physical wooden image, not the awakened person/teaching-seat figure covered by the standalone ‘buddha’ (佛) entry. This is therefore a required family cross-check, but not a second sense of the fixed case title: every occurrence names the same burning case. The guide identifies this among possible precept-violation cases; the harvested passages supply rebuke, ‘the deed is not light,’ and cause-and-effect warnings, but none explicitly names a particular precept. The entry therefore reports those attestations without asserting an unattested precept charge.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Empty Valley Collection labels this ‘case twenty-five: Danxia burns the buddha’ and opens its instruction: ‘when hot seek cool; when cold face the fire—also ordinary.’

Occurrences.Kwic: 頌丹霞燒佛，曰：丹霞燒佛業非輕，院主眉鬚火裏生。自作從來還自受，孰言因果不分明？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later verse says: ‘Danxia's burning the buddha was no light deed; the officer's eyebrows and beard grow in the fire. What one does, one has always received; who says cause and effect are unclear?’
